judgment: comment -> video relation does not exist in the current corpus; 0% of product reviews can be tied to a video_id
reason: The 175 canonical tiktok_shop records are product reviews fetched from /api/v1/tiktok/shop/web/fetch_product_reviews_v2. Their external_id is the review_id (it matches raw review_id 175/175), not a video/aweme id. Neither the canonical source_meta nor the 180 raw review rows expose video_id/aweme_id/item_id. The reviewer_id in the raw payload is the review author's user id, not a video author id. Therefore a comment->video relation cannot be built from this corpus. This is a product-review layer, not a video-comment layer.

evidence.canonical_external_id_shape: 19-digit numeric string; matches raw review_id 175/175 and does not collide with any of the 141 video IDs
evidence.reviewer_id_role: review author user id; not a video id, aweme id, or video creator id
evidence.canonical_author_field: masked reviewer name, not a TikTok creator unique_id

why_the_layer_is_different.product_review: a review of a product, keyed by review_id + product_id + sku_id
why_the_layer_is_different.video_comment: a comment under a video, keyed by comment_id + aweme_id
why_the_layer_is_different.population_mismatch: the review layer and the video/comment layer have different populations and different denominators; do not merge them

what_would_be_needed: A product-review payload that includes video_id/aweme_id/item_id (the current TikTok Shop review endpoint does not expose it).
Or an affiliate/order attribution export that maps review_id or order_id to the promoting video.
Or switch to fetch_video_comments, which returns comments keyed by aweme_id, and treat them as a separate video-comment population.
A product->video enumeration source (creator cookie endpoint or a verified product-video index) to connect the review product to videos.
what_was_not_done: No reviewer_id was treated as a creator_id or video_id.
No canonical-records.jsonl or gold-set-50.jsonl content was changed.
